problem:
The matrix $A$ is given below. Let ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$,  ${a}_{3}$ and ${a}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $A.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(A).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${a}_{4}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$ 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 & 4 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
The matrix $H$ is given below. Let ${h}_{1}$, ${h}_{2}$,  ${h}_{3}$ and ${h}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $H.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{h}_{1},{h}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(H).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${h}_{4}={x}_{1}{h}_{1}+{x}_{2}{h}_{2}.$ 

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 12 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $H$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}H & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 12 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(H)$ is ${{h}_{1},{h}_{2},{h}_{3}}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B={{h}_{1},{h}_{2}}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(H).$
